gate: ADR-0005 Intel Arc B580 dynamic-method spike
model: OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct Q4_K_M (4018.3 MB; base allenai URL timed out, instruct fallback used; same file across all cases)

criteria.1_it_runs: PASS - all three cases generated coherent text
criteria.2_ran_on_gpu: PASS - arc cases 34/34 layers on Vulkan, 0 on CPU; CPU control is the mirror image (0 Vulkan / 34 CPU). No silent fallback.
criteria.3_method_applied: PASS - arc_topk4 reports n_expert_used=4 from llama.cpp itself (override honoured)
criteria.4_named_ceiling: PASS - active-expert throughput on the GPU. Model fully VRAM-resident (4 GB in 12 GB, 34/34 offloaded) so not disk- or host-RAM-bound; halving active experts (8->4) gave ~3.86x decode speedup (88.1->340.4 t/s), which only an active-expert-dominated binder produces.
criteria.5_reference_stated: PASS - fidelity measured as backend divergence, not identity. arc_topk8 vs cpu_topk8 (same file, same box, top-8, seed 0) share 'The capital of France is Paris. Paris is not only the political' then diverge (arc: 'capital...'; cpu: ', but also the economic...'). Cross-backend divergence is expected (reduction order / kernels) and is the deliverable, not a failure.

method_effect_note: top-k 8->4 was ~3.86x faster AND stayed coherent/correct, but this is 48 tokens of ONE prompt - it is NOT a quality claim. Quality-vs-active-compute needs a real perplexity/benchmark eval, which is the benchmark v1's job, not this spike's.
consequence: Arc leg viable. Authorises SCOPING a three-vendor benchmark v1 as a separate effort with its own gate, timeline-permitting (relocation Q4 2026). Does NOT authorise open-ended benchmark work.
